step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture describes a migration from on-premise IBM Netezza databases to an AWS Redshift data warehouse, emphasizing an ELT (Extract, Load, Transform) process. Data is ingested from on-prem databases via Storage Gateway and Direct Connect into an S3 Landing Zone. EC2 instances perform quality cleansing and transformation, using metadata and scripts stored in an RDS PostgreSQL database. The processed data moves through an S3 Transformation bucket, is loaded into Redshift, and finally published to an S3 Publish bucket, with older data archived to Glacier. Users access Redshift for ad-hoc queries and the S3 Publish bucket for daily dashboards.

graph.name: Life Sciences Data Migration to Redshift with ELT
graph.categories: Data Lake, Analytics, Migration, ELT, Data Warehouse
graph.notes: This architecture focuses on migrating data from on-prem IBM Netezza to AWS Redshift, leveraging Storage Gateway and Direct Connect for ingestion. An ELT process is implemented using EC2 instances and S3 buckets for staging and transformation, orchestrated by metadata in RDS. Retention policies are applied across S3 buckets, with Glacier used for long-term archiving. The architecture is HIPAA compliant with encryption at rest and in transit.

nodes.name: IBM Netezza Databases
nodes.notes: Source databases located on-premise for life sciences client data.

nodes.name: Storage Gateway
nodes.notes: Ingests daily incremental data (100 GB) from on-prem databases using NFS volumes. Data is encrypted with AES256.

nodes.name: Direct Connect
nodes.notes: Provides a dedicated 2x10Gb network connection between on-premise and AWS, secured with SSL encryption.

nodes.name: S3 Landing Zone
nodes.notes: Initial landing zone for ingested data from on-prem. Data is encrypted at rest (AES256). Retention period: 2 days.

nodes.name: Quality Cleansing EC2 Instances
nodes.notes: EC2 instances that pick up scripts from RDS to perform data quality and cleansing on data from the S3 Landing Zone.

nodes.name: RDS (Postgres)
nodes.notes: Stores metadata and ELT transformation scripts, deployed on PostgreSQL, with a future migration plan to Aurora.

nodes.name: S3 Transformation Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores data after quality cleansing, awaiting further transformation. Retention period: 1 day. Data is encrypted at rest (AES256).

nodes.name: Transformation EC2 Instances
nodes.notes: EC2 instances that transform data from the S3 Transformation Bucket into facts and dimensions, using scripts from RDS, before loading into Redshift.

nodes.name: Redshift
nodes.notes: Target data warehouse for transformed data. Initial schema setup used AWS Schema Conversion Tool. Users access via Redshift Spectrum for ad-hoc reports.

nodes.name: S3 Publish Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores published data from Redshift, used for daily dashboards. Retention period: 1 year and 1 month. Data is encrypted at rest (AES256).

nodes.name: Glacier
nodes.notes: Archival storage for data from the S3 Publish bucket after its retention period.

nodes.name: Business Users/Analysts
nodes.notes: Access Redshift for ad-hoc reports via Redshift Spectrum and S3 Publish for daily dashboards. Also represents developers.

edges.notes: On-premise databases send daily incremental data to Storage Gateway.
Storage Gateway ingests data into AWS via Direct Connect.
Data flows from Direct Connect into the S3 Landing Zone.
EC2 instances for Quality Cleansing retrieve data from the S3 Landing Zone.
EC2 Quality Cleansing instances access metadata and scripts from RDS.
RDS provides metadata and scripts to EC2 Quality Cleansing instances.
Cleansed data is pushed by EC2 Quality Cleansing instances to the S3 Transformation Bucket.
EC2 Transformation instances retrieve data from the S3 Transformation Bucket.
EC2 Transformation instances access metadata and scripts from RDS.
RDS provides metadata and scripts to EC2 Transformation instances.
Transformed data is loaded by EC2 Transformation instances into Redshift.
Redshift publishes processed data to the S3 Publish Bucket.
Aged data from S3 Publish is moved to Glacier for archival after its retention period.
Users query Redshift for ad-hoc reports via Redshift Spectrum.
Redshift returns query results to users.
Users access the S3 Publish Bucket for daily dashboards and data.
S3 Publish bucket serves dashboard data to users.
RDS provides schema and metadata information to Redshift (e.g., for initial setup or ongoing schema management, as per visual).
Redshift provides status or metadata updates back to RDS (as per visual).
